style: An ancient Chinese fable unfolding in a moonlit courtyard. Natural, intimate cinematic delivery with restrained ironic warmth; never childish, broad, or commercial. Leave a small breath at the end of every line.

speakers.name: Narrator
speakers.style: A mature storyteller with a low warm voice, precise observation, and very dry humor.

speakers.name: Thief
speakers.style: A furtive young man who is far too pleased with his own cleverness; lively but never cartoonish.

speakers.name: Villager
speakers.style: An alert adult woman calling firmly from beyond the courtyard wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Long ago, a man found a magnificent bronze bell hanging in a quiet courtyard.
lines.direction: Invite the listener into the moonlit setting; give bronze bell quiet importance.

lines.speaker: Thief
lines.text: A bell this fine ought to belong to me.
lines.direction: Hushed, selfish, and certain, as if the thought settles the matter.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He pulled with all his strength. The bell did not move at all.
lines.direction: Build the effort, then land the second sentence with dry restraint.

lines.speaker: Thief
lines.text: Too heavy to carry... I'll break it apart and take it piece by piece.
lines.direction: Frustrated first; after the pause, delighted by his terrible idea.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He lifted his hammer and struck.
lines.direction: Tighten the pace and end crisply, leaving room for the bell impact.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The bell's voice leapt over the courtyard wall and rolled far into the night.
lines.direction: Open the voice outward; let far into the night carry a long resonance.

lines.speaker: Thief
lines.text: Oh no! Everyone will hear it!
lines.direction: Genuinely alarmed but controlled; do not shriek.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: In a panic, he clapped both hands over his ears. The courtyard fell silent—at least, for him.
lines.direction: Urgent first sentence; a knowing trace of amusement after the dash.

lines.speaker: Thief
lines.text: Ha! If I cannot hear it, no one else can either.
lines.direction: Quietly triumphant, completely confident in absurd logic.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pleased with his cleverness, he struck again. The second peal was louder than the first.
lines.direction: Understated irony; make the final sentence clean and emphatic.

lines.speaker: Villager
lines.direction: A sudden, firm call from outside the courtyard.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The neighbors followed the sound and caught him beside the bell. He had fooled his own ears, but not the world. We remember it as covering one's ears while stealing a bell.
lines.direction: A swift satisfying resolution without lecturing; slow slightly over the final phrase.
